In the original DeepWalk method, vertex sequences are modeled with SkipGram, not with an LSTM. Under your hypothetical modification, DeepWalk would treat each random-walk vertex sequence as an input sequence to a recurrent network, and the LSTM cell state would be updated at each time step t using the standard gated recurrence:

- Forget gate: f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t + U_f h_{t-1} + b_f)
- Input gate: i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t + U_i h_{t-1} + b_i)
- Candidate cell content: \tilde{c}_t = \tanh(W_c x_t + U_c h_{t-1} + b_c)
- Cell state update: c_t = f_t \odot c_{t-1} + i_t \odot \tilde{c}_t
- Output gate: o_t = \sigma(W_o x_t + U_o h_{t-1} + b_o)
- Hidden state: h_t = o_t \odot \tanh(c_t)

Here, x_t is the input representation of the current vertex in the walk, h_{t-1} is the previous hidden state, c_{t-1} is the previous cell state, \sigma is the logistic sigmoid, and \odot denotes elementwise multiplication. If Backpropagation Through Time were used, gradients would be propagated through these recurrent updates across the unrolled walk sequence. This is a hypothetical LSTM-based variant of DeepWalk; it is not the original DeepWalk formulation.
